rationale: The provided literature contradicts the foundational claims of the hypothesis. Rather than an 18-proband series by Parenti et al., the published Parenti et al. (2020) study reported only a single proband with Cornelia de Lange syndrome caused by a MAU2 variant. Furthermore, that single proband explicitly manifested very early gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Subsequent literature (Peng et al., 2024) similarly confirms that up to that time only a single MAU2-CdLS case had been reported worldwide by Parenti et al. No evidence in the available sources supports the existence of an 18-proband series evaluating surgical intervention rates for GI malformations or intractable GERD in MAU2-CdLS.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. (2020) reported a single proband with Cornelia de Lange syndrome caused by a MAU2 variant who developed very early gastroesophageal reflux disease, rather than describing an 18-individual cohort.

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts an 18-proband series from Parenti et al. with fewer than 20% (under 4 of 18) experiencing severe GI malformations or GERD requiring surgery, whereas the actual Parenti et al. (2020) publication and independent reviews cite only 1 MAU2 proband who presented with early gastroesophageal reflux disease.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and severity of gastrointestinal anomalies and gastroesophageal reflux disease across an expanded international registry of confirmed MAU2 pathogenic variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Because only isolated case reports currently exist in the indexed literature, multi-center registry aggregation is needed to establish whether GI phenotypes discriminate MAU2-CdLS from NIPBL-associated CdLS.
